messages:
Marta (Finance): Hey all — heads-up that starting next pay period we'll tighten the approval chain for vendor onboarding and large one-off charges. Summary: default p-card limit stays, but any single vendor charge >= $12,000 needs Director+Finance signoff; vendor onboarding requests must include a completed intake form and tax docs; unanswered vendor requests older than 7 days will be auto-escalated. Please read the short policy on the intranet.

Diego (Eng): Does this change team-level monthly thresholds or just single-charge rules?

Marta (Finance): Just single-charge threshold and onboarding process. Monthly aggregated spend caps remain as-is. Team monthly increases still go through manager + finance.

Asha (People Ops): Quick reminder for recruiting teams: agency contracts often hit that threshold. Make sure recruiting ops fills the procurement intake early.

Diego (Eng): If we need to expedite a vendor (e.g., critical bug fix), what's the fastest route?

Marta (Finance): Use the "expedite-onboard" tag on the intake form and email finance@redwood with justification. Procurement will triage and aim for a 48-hour turnaround for true emergencies. Abuse will be reviewed.

ProcurementBot: New requirement: please attach W-9/merchant tax form to all vendor intake submissions. Missing docs will delay onboarding. Link: https://intranet.redwood/finance/vendor-intake

Marta (Finance): We'll run a weekly vendor intake report and notify owners of stale requests. Reach out if you need clarifications — I'll post the one-pager guide in #announcements shortly. :memo:
